title: The Community Garden Meeting
instructions: 阅读下面的短文，完成10道题目。题目类型包括单选、填空和判断正误/未提及。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。请仔细阅读短文，答案必须基于原文。本材料为模拟教育材料，不是官方雅思考试。
passage:
Last Tuesday, the Maple Street Community Centre held a meeting about a new garden project. About forty people attended. The meeting was friendly, but people had very different ideas. The discussion showed how communities often need to balance different needs, such as safe places for children and support for local businesses. It also showed that when people listen to each other, they can often find a compromise that works for most of them.

A. The first speaker was Mrs. Chen, who has lived on Maple Street for thirty years. She said, "We need a garden because children have no safe place to play." She also said that the old parking lot behind the centre is ugly and dangerous. "Although the lot is small, we can grow vegetables and flowers there," she explained. Many parents agreed with her. They said the garden would give children a place to learn about nature and spend time outside. Some of them added that children today spend too much time indoors, and a garden would give them fresh air and exercise.

B. Next, Mr. Patel spoke. He owns a small shop on the corner. He said, "I understand the plan, but we need parking spaces because customers cannot stop here." He added, "While I like gardens, my business is important too." Some shop owners nodded. They said the parking lot is necessary because of the many cars on the street. Without parking, they worried that customers would go to other shops. Mr. Patel explained that many of his customers drive to the area, and if they cannot park nearby, they will simply shop somewhere else.

C. Then Ms. Rivera, a teacher, offered a solution. "We can use half the lot for a garden and half for parking," she said. "Because of the limited space, we must share." She suggested that the garden could have raised beds and that parking could be for short stays only. Most people liked this idea, but Mr. Patel was not sure. He wanted to know how the parking would be controlled. Ms. Rivera suggested that a simple sign could explain the rules, and that volunteers could help keep an eye on the lot.

D. Finally, the group voted. They decided to try Ms. Rivera's plan for six months. Mrs. Chen was happy because the children will have a garden. Mr. Patel agreed to wait and see. The meeting ended with tea and biscuits. Everyone promised to meet again in September to talk about how the plan is working. They also agreed to write down any problems during the trial period so that the next meeting could be more useful.

grammar.title: 主题句与支持句；although / while；because 与 because of
grammar.explanation: 在段落写作中，主题句（topic sentence）表达段落的主要观点，支持句（supporting sentences）提供细节、例子或原因来支持主题句。例如，主题句：'We need a garden because children have no safe place to play.' 支持句：'Although the lot is small, we can grow vegetables and flowers there.' 连接词 although 和 while 用于引导让步状语从句，表示对比或转折，后面接完整的句子（主语+谓语）。because 后面接从句（主语+谓语），而 because of 后面接名词或名词短语。例如：'Because of the limited space, we must share.' 中 because of 后接名词短语 the limited space。注意：although 和 while 不能与 but 连用。
grammar.example: Although the lot is small, we can grow vegetables and flowers there.

questions.explanation: while 表示对比，虽然我喜欢咖啡，但早上更喜欢茶。
questions.evidence: While I like gardens, my business is important too.
